name: Texas Instruments
key_signal: TXN has broken below its 50-day moving average with a negative MACD histogram and negative 21-day momentum, even as it trades at a stretched 49x trailing / 30x forward P/E after a 54% run over six months.
thesis: TXN's underlying fundamentals remain excellent — 18.6% revenue growth, 31% earnings growth, 37.8% operating margins, and 32% ROE reflect genuine analog/embedded chip demand recovery and pricing power, with the stock still comfortably above its 200-day SMA (220.6) and in a golden-cross uptrend. If the semiconductor cycle continues to inflect upward, TXN's premium multiple could be justified by continued double-digit earnings growth, and the current pullback from the 334 high to 288 offers a re-entry point within a structurally bullish trend for long-term holders (32 analysts rate it 'buy').
bear_case: The technical picture has clearly deteriorated in the last month: price is down 4.6% over 21 days, sitting below the 50-day SMA (301) with a deepening negative MACD histogram (-2.1) and RSI at a lukewarm 45, all signaling loss of near-term momentum after an unsustainable 54% six-month run. At the same time, valuation is extreme for a cyclical semiconductor name — 49x trailing earnings, 15.6x book value, and 83.7% debt-to-equity — leaving little room for error if analog/industrial demand growth decelerates or if the broader semi-cycle rolls over, and the stock's elevated 60% annualized volatility plus 1.31 beta mean any disappointment could trigger an outsized correction toward the 200-day SMA near 220, roughly 24% below current price.
